name: Single-Arm Incline Dumbbell Flye
description: A unilateral isolation movement performed on an incline bench, targeting the clavicular (upper) fibers of the pectoralis major. Using one arm at a time allows for a greater range of motion, enhanced mind-muscle connection, and identification and correction of left-right strength imbalances. The non-working arm can hold the bench edge for stability.

execution.starting_position: Lie on an incline bench set to 30–45 degrees. Hold one dumbbell in the working hand above the upper chest with a slight bend in the elbow. The opposite hand grips the bench edge for stability.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the incline to 30–45 degrees. Select a dumbbell lighter than you would use for a bilateral flye since there is no counterbalancing load on the other side.
steps: Step 1: Begin with the working arm extended above the upper chest, palm facing inward.
Step 2: Lower the dumbbell out to the side in a wide arc, maintaining the fixed elbow bend. Feel the deep stretch across the upper chest.
Step 3: At full stretch, reverse the arc and bring the dumbbell back above the chest.
Step 4: Squeeze the pectoral at the top. Repeat all reps, then switch sides.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale as you lower the dumbbell. Exhale as you bring it back up.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbow bend excessively during the movement, turning it into a press
Rotating the torso toward the working arm — keep hips and shoulders flat on the bench
Using too heavy a dumbbell, compromising shoulder stability
safety_considerations: Use a spotter or place the non-working hand on the bench edge for stability
Control the descent carefully — the shoulder is vulnerable at end-range with single-arm load
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Open to the furthest comfortable stretch — typically when the upper arm is parallel to the bench surface or slightly below.
coaching_cues: Lead with the elbow, not the hand — keep the arc wide
Think of hugging a barrel with one arm — the motion is a sweep, not a curl
